**Solution Overview**

The recurrence can be factored:

\[
a_{n+1}=a_n^{3}+5a_n^{2}+10a_n+6
      =(a_n+1)(a_n^{2}+4a_n+6).
\]

Consider the sequence  

\[
b_n=\frac{2^{n}}{a_n+2}.
\]

Compute the difference:

\[
\begin{aligned}
b_n-b_{n+1}
&=\frac{2^{n}}{a_n+2}-\frac{2^{n+1}}{a_{n+1}+2}
   =2^{n}\!\left[\frac{1}{a_n+2}-\frac{2}{a_{n+1}+2}\right] \\
&=2^{n}\frac{a_{n+1}-2a_n-2}{(a_n+2)(a_{n+1}+2)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using the factorisation of \(a_{n+1}\),

\[
a_{n+1}-2a_n-2
   =(a_n+1)(a_n+2)^2,
\]

so

\[
b_n-b_{n+1}=2^{n}\frac{(a_n+1)(a_n+2)}{a_{n+1}+2}.
\]

But from the recurrence we also have  

\[
a_{n+1}+2=(a_n+2)(a_n^{2}+3a_n+4),
\]

hence

\[
b_n-b_{n+1}=2^{n}\frac{a_n+1}{a_n^{2}+3a_n+4}.
\]

Thus each term of the required series equals the telescoping difference \(b_n-b_{n+1}\). Therefore

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{2^{n}(a_n+1)}{a_n^{2}+3a_n+4}
   =\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(b_n-b_{n+1})
   =b_0-\lim_{n\to\infty}b_n.
\]

Now  

\[
b_0=\frac{2^{0}}{a_0+2}=\frac{1}{2024+2}=\frac{1}{2026},
\]

and because \(a_{n+1}\approx a_n^{3}\) the denominator \(a_n+2\) grows far faster than \(2^{n}\); consequently \(\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}b_n=0\).

Hence the infinite sum equals \(\frac{1}{2026}\).

**Answer**

ANSWER: 1/2026
